eligibility.why: The verified article is a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected, athletic-trainer surveillance. Soccer-specific concussion counts, athlete-exposures and rates are directly reported by sex.

source.citation: Hacherl SL, Herman DC, Martin JR, et al. Sex Differences in Concussion Rates among Middle School Sex-comparable Sports. The Journal of Pediatrics: Clinical Practice. 2026;20:200200. doi:10.1016/j.jpedcp.2026.200200.

stageA.populationRule: Use the only directly reported football-specific split: Girls' soccer / Boys' soccer. Do not add a Total row, because the article does not print a pooled soccer row. Do not use the 11,213 all-sport athlete count as a soccer sample size.

definitions.injuryDefinition: medical attention [clinically diagnosed sport-related concussion requiring removal from activity]

evidence.supports: Citation, prospective epidemiological design, Virginia 2015-2022, athletic-trainer collection, athlete-exposure denominator and soccer as an included sport.

Retrospective research using embedded certified athletic trainers, daily SportsWare documentation, daily attendance by sport, athlete-exposure definition, and the four-part clinically diagnosed concussion definition.
Sex-comparison IRRs and a visual duplicate of Table II rates. These comparison estimates are reviewed but not mapped into a Tabs 1-10 field.

Soccer mechanism rows. Girls: player 8, surface 5, equipment 1, ball 7, nonspecific 9, unknown 1. Boys: player 6, surface 1, equipment 0, ball 6, nonspecific 4, unknown 1. injuryContact is the transparent direct sum of the five explicitly contact-classified categories: 30 / 17. Unknown is intentionally excluded.

participantCharacteristics: meanAge: reported only for the whole mixed-sport cohort, not soccer-specific
numberOfTeams: school counts are not football-team counts
definitions: illnessDefinition, burdenDefinition, severityDefinition, recurrenceDefinition: not reported
exposure: seasonLength, numberOfSeasons: no compatible direct numeric season field is reported for the soccer subgroup
injuryOutcome: injuryPlayersCompletedStudy, injuryTeamsCompletedStudy, all medical-attention/time-loss subcounts, all time-loss incidence fields, burden/time-loss/severity fields, most-common fields, onset fields, injuryNonContact, injuryCumulativeRepetitive, recurrence fields: not separately reported or not a clean schema mapping
The soccer cohort is concussion-specific, so no generic most-common diagnosis/type/location is echoed.
injuryTissueType: All fields other than concussion prevalence: no tissue/type table, severity, burden or subtype value.
injuryLocation: All fields: concussion is a diagnosis here; no body-location table or direct location result is reported.

reviewerCaveats: This is a football-specific subgroup within a multi-sport study. Retain only the soccer rows, not pooled multi-sport totals.
The source calls the study prospective but says the research was retrospective. The proposed design records both facts.
The paper has a missing 2020-2021 school-year sport period, so no unsupported numeric season count is staged.
Confirm the amendment gate and current paper assignment before any live apply.
